item.title: UK to adopt tougher stance on Israel with illegal settlements trade ban
item.description: Ed Miliband to reassert support for Palestinian rights and a two-state solution in move likely to draw fierce criticism from US and Israel Ed Miliband will announce what he has described as a broad reset of the UK’s relations with Israel on Tuesday, promising the government will take a more active approach in supporting the Palestinian cause. In an intervention that is expected to draw fierce criticism from the US and Israel, the foreign secretary will impose a UK ban on the trade in goods and some services from illegal Israeli settlements. item.title: Israel recrudece sus ataques contra Líbano y deja a varias personas muertas
item.description: Una nueva noche de ataques israelíes en Líbano. Los bombardeos alcanzaron una aldea en el sur del país y mataron a varias personas, en un operativo llevado a cabo en respuesta a ataques de Hezbolá, según justificó Israel. Desde el pasado viernes, Israel multiplica sus ataques contra el sur de la nación árabe, considerada un bastión del grupo chiita, pese al acuerdo marco firmado entre Israel y Líbano en junio. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: La cresta de Ali Al-Taher, trasfondo de los mortíferos ataques de Israel en el sur de Líbano
item.description: En el sur de Líbano, Israel sigue atacando duramente la región de Nabatiyeh. Este 7 de septiembre, más de una decena de personas murieron en bombardeos israelíes, entre ellos, bebés y paramédicos. Israel justifica su ofensiva asegurando que está dirigida a Hezbolá en represalia por otros ataques del grupo chiita; sin embargo, no es posible verificar la información de manera independiente. Nos amplía la información nuestra corresponsal, Janira Gómez Muñoz. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: North Korea and Russia open their first road bridge, a symbol of expanding ties
item.description: Connection across Tumen River is further sign of closer ties between the two countries since start of war in Ukraine Russia and North Korea have opened the first road bridge across their shared border , in the latest sign of the rapidly deepening ties between the two countries since the start of the war in Ukraine. The one-kilometre bridge spans the Tumen River between Khasan in Russia’s far east and Tumangang in North Korea, along a remote and sparsely populated stretch of the countries’ shared border just a few miles from the coast. Continue reading... Publicado también por: South China Morning Post, ABC News Australia, The Guardian - World. Fuente: The Jerusalem Post - International.

item.title: Syrian reactor could have been used for nuclear weapons if completed, UN says
item.description: Chief of nuclear watchdog says secret Assad-era facility would have been able to produce fissile material A nearly complete nuclear reactor built secretly during the rule of the toppled Syrian leader Bashar al-Assad would have been able to produce fissile material for possible use in nuclear weapons, the chief of the UN nuclear watchdog has revealed. Inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) last month visited two sites, one in Deir ez-Zor and a second in an undisclosed location identified to them by Syrian authorities.
